entries.citation: Mahajan, K. & Nandhini S. (14 Oct 2024). Restart: Women, career breaks and employer response. Ashoka University, Department of Economics, Discussion Paper No. 125.
entries.venue: Ashoka University, Dept. of Economics, Discussion Paper No. 125 (working paper)

headline.label: lower callback rate for women with a career break than comparable women without one

findings: Women who take a career break receive 49% lower callbacks than otherwise similar women without a break.
Simply listing upskilling certifications does not produce a statistically significant difference in callbacks for women with a break.
The penalty is larger in skill-intensive sectors such as finance, in smaller firms, and in firms located in north India.
limits: Working paper, not yet a peer-reviewed journal article.
Women only; Anchor does not assume the penalty applies equally to every individual.
Penalty size varies by sector, firm size and region.
entries.transferability_note: Run in the Indian private sector, the closest match to Anchor's target market. Sector and region effects mean the average is a prior, not a prediction.

entries.citation: Kristal, A. S., Nicks, L., Gloor, J. L. & Hauser, O. P. (2022). Reducing discrimination against job seekers with and without employment gaps. Nature Human Behaviour, 7(2), 211-218. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-022-01485-6
entries.authors: Ariella S. Kristal; Leonie Nicks; Jamie L. Gloor; Oliver P. Hauser
entries.study_type: Preregistered audit field experiment, plus lab studies (N = 2,650)

headline.label: more callbacks when a resume shows years worked instead of employment dates, versus resumes showing gaps

findings: Listing previous jobs with the number of years worked, instead of employment dates, increased callbacks by about 15% compared with resumes showing employment gaps.
Compared with resumes without gaps, the same reframing increased callbacks by about 8%.
Lab studies found the effect holds for female and male applicants and for applicants with less and more total experience.
The effect is driven by making the applicant's job experience salient, not by novelty or ease of reading.
limits: Field experiment run in the United Kingdom; transfer to the Indian labour market is not established.
Reported as a percentage increase in callbacks; Anchor applies it as a relative (multiplicative) lift.
Population-level result, not a guarantee for an individual application.
entries.transferability_note: UK result. Anchor uses it as a population-level prior and shows the geography limitation on screen.
